thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager duty: svc-ingest proxy abnormal header pattern detected (rate: 1.2k/min) — alert id 9f3d

sarah: Ack. I'm on call. seeing the same in edge logs, looks like header X-External-Auth has base64 blob repeating.

mike: Any customer impact reported?

sarah: No 5xx but some auth failures from internal indexer jobs. Not user-facing yet.

jordan: Is it definitely sensitive? Could be telemetry. Attach sample.

sarah: sample (redacted):
```
X-External-Auth: YWJjMTIzIT8kKiQoKS1yZWxheWVkLXJlcG9fa2V5Cg==
X-Trace: abc-123
```

carla: That Base64 decodes to a short token-like payload w/ punctuation. Looks like a session fragment. Recommend contain and key rotation.

mike: +1 on containment. Steps?

sarah: Proposed steps: 1) Isolate svc-ingest from internet egress (temp rule) 2) Block the source IPs 3) Rotate any service tokens seen in the sample 4) Kick off customer-impact check 5) Legal/PR notif hold.

jordan: Can we confirm origin? I see a kinesis shard emitting malformed headers from staging-proxy-3 around 01:12 UTC.

pagerbot: Incident severity set to P1 by monitoring rule (auth-leakage-pattern). Paging security on-call.

security-bot: @carla assigned as security lead. Notifying CISO.

carla: I'll lead. Sarah, can you snapshot the logs and preserve full request bodies to S3 with restricted ACL? Tag path /incidents/1977027000/

sarah: Done. Uploaded bucket: s3://redwood-incident-collector/1977027000/logs (acl:internal-only).

mike: I'm going to add an ACL to ingest-proxy to block external egress and remove outbound S3 roles for that service. Pushing policy in infra now.

jordan: Applying firewall rule: deny egress for svc-ingest-prod until further notice. Command: `infractl firewall update svc-ingest --deny-egress=true`

carla: Good. Next: rotate service tokens used by ingest workers. We need a list of candidate secrets found in logs. Sarah, paste redacted list.

sarah: Found 3 token fragments across requests: tkn-xx1, tkn-yy2, tkn-zz3 (redacted). I triggered creds rotate for svc-ingest role in IAM, new keys issuing.

security-bot: Rotation job started (job id rot-1977027000-1). ETA ~7m.

mike: I've paused any background batch jobs that call third-party indexer to avoid replay. `jobs pause --tag ingest-batch`

carla: Customer impact check: billing+support — any customers with increased auth errors?

sarah: Quick query: auth.failure{service:ingest} shows a small blip affecting internal tenants but no high-severity customer errors. Not seeing external client 401 surge.

jordan: Forensics: copying headers to internal SIEM, correlating with deploy events. No recent deploy to ingest in last 12h.

mike: Rotation complete for IAM role svc-ingest-role. Confirmed new keys in KMS.

security-bot: Rotation job completed (rot-1977027000-1) status: success. All old tokens revoked.

carla: Nice. Next: run a quick audit for S3 exposures — check public buckets for similar fragments. Sarah, run `s3scan --pattern "YWJj"`

sarah: Running now. Found one archived dev artifact with matching string in path, removed public ACL, queued for scrub.

mike: Re-enable batched jobs with new creds once we've validated no leaked tokens remain and customer-facing traffic is stable.

carla: Agreed. I'll prepare a short incident note for legal & customer-facing teams. We need to decide on disclosure threshold — likely internal-only but prepping comms in case.

jordan: Suggest follow-ups: 1) Add stricter header validation at edge 2) Mask tokens in logs at ingestion 3) Add unit test for header sanitizer 4) Postmortem in 48h.

carla: Assigning follow-ups: Sarah (logs scrub + retention policy), Mike (infra egress rules + deploy sanitizer), Jordan (forensics writeup). I'll tag security-announce draft and loop legal.

pagerbot: Incident status: Contained. Severity -> P2. Handoff complete.

carla: Thanks team. Closing on-call for now; reopening if we see replay or customer impact. :thumbsup:
